## Q1
1.
```{r}
x <- c(NA, rnorm(n=20))
fivenum(x)
fivenum(x)[4] - fivenum(x)[2]
```

2.
```{r}
f <- function(x) {
  return(fivenum(x)[4] - fivenum(x)[2])
}

y <- c(NA, rnorm(n=67))
z <- c(NA, rnorm(n=100))
f(x); f(y); f(z)
```

3.
```{r}
IQR(x, na.rm = TRUE); IQR(y, na.rm = TRUE); IQR(z, na.rm = TRUE)
```

4.
```{r}
CompHinge <- function(n) {
  x <- c(NA, rnorm(n = n))

  f(x) - IQR(x, na.rm = TRUE)
}

diff1<- replicate(1000, CompHinge(20))

diff2 <- replicate(1000, CompHinge(200))
diff3 <- replicate(1000, CompHinge(2000))
```

```{r}
hist(diff1, main = "n = 20", xlab = "Hinge diff - IQR")

hist(diff2, main = "n = 200", xlab = "Hinge diff - IQR")

hist(diff3, main = "n = 2000", xlab = "Hinge diff - IQR")
```

5.
As the sample size n increased,
the differences between the two functions approached 0, 
but the two functions aren't perfectly identical


## Q2
1 & 2.
```{r}
set.seed(23453144)
X <- matrix(runif(n = 15, min = -10, max = 10),nrow = 3, ncol = 5)
X
```

3 & 4.
```{r}
X_svd <- svd(X)

U <- X_svd$u
V <- X_svd$v

D <- diag(X_svd$d)

U; V; D
```

5.
```{r}
UD <- U %*% D

X_new <- tcrossprod(UD, V)
all.equal(X, X_new)
```

6.
```{r}
VD <-  tcrossprod(V, D)

all.equal(crossprod(X), tcrossprod(VD))
```

## Q3
1 & 2.
```{r}
set.seed(999)

x1 <- gl(2, 100)
x2 <- runif(200)

y <- c( rnorm(n = 100, mean = 20 - 0.5*x2[1:100], sd = 3),
  rnorm(n = 100, mean = 10 - 0.5*x2[101:200], sd = 3))
```

3.
```{r}
X <- model.matrix(y ~ x1 + x2)


beta_LS3 <- function(X, y) {
  solve(crossprod(X), crossprod(X, y))
  }

beta_hat <- beta_LS3(X, y)
beta_hat
```

4.
```{r}
t1 <- crossprod(y) #all terms of numerator
t2 <- crossprod(y, X %*% beta_hat)
t3 <- crossprod(beta_hat, crossprod(X, y))
t4 <- crossprod(beta_hat, crossprod(X) %*% beta_hat)

(t1 - t2 - t3 + t4) / 197; anova(lm(y ~ x1 + x2))$"Mean Sq"[3]
```

5.
```{r}

mse <- anova(lm(y ~ x1 + x2))$"Mean Sq"[3]

H <- solve(crossprod(X)) * as.numeric(mse)

sqrt(diag(H)); sqrt(diag(vcov(lm(y ~ x1 + x2))))
```

6.
```{r}
y <- c(10, 9, 4, 5, 14, 20, 20, 19, 7)
x1 <- c(7, 3, 5, 0, 2, -6, -4, -6, -1)
x2 <- c(-4, -1, -1, 4, 6, 1, 0, -5, 0)

X <- model.matrix(y ~ x1 + x2)
XtX <- crossprod(X)
XtX

XtXi <- solve(XtX)
XtXi
```

```{r}
beta_LS4 <- function(X, y) {
  crossprod(X, y) / diag(crossprod(X))
}

beta_LS3(X, y); beta_LS4(X, y)

```

```{r}
library(microbenchmark)

microbenchmark(
  beta_LS3 = beta_LS3(X, y),
  beta_LS4 = beta_LS4(X, y),
  times = 1000)
```

## Q4
1.
```{r}
e4 <- runif(10000)

csum <- function(x) {
  if(length(x) == 1) return(x)
  
  sumx <- x[1]
  for(i in seq(2, length(x))) {
    sumx[i] <- sum(x[1:i])
  }
  sumx
}

out <- csum(e4)
all.equal(out, cumsum(e4))
```
<iframe src="profvis_output.html" width="100%" height="600px" frameborder="0" scrolling="yes"></iframe>


The function sum() is repeated inside the loop for every single iteration of the for loop
x[1:i] repeatedly calls a vector that's constantly increasing
Calculating basically the same sum over and over again 
takes up too much time 

```{r}
csum2 <- function(x) {
  if(length(x) == 1) return(x)
  
  sumx <- numeric(length(x)) 
  # create blank vector with same length ONCE to use 

  temp <- x[1]
  sumx[1] <- temp

  #add ONE new value at each iteration
  for (i in seq(2, length(x))) {
    temp <- temp + x[i]
    sumx[i] <- temp
  }
  sumx
}

out <- csum2(e4)
all.equal(out, cumsum(e4))
```

```{r}
 time <- microbenchmark(csum = csum(e4),
                csum2 = csum2(e4),
                cumsum = cumsum(e4),times = 10)

time2 <- summary(time)
time2
((time2$median[1] - time2$median[2])/time2$median[1]) * 100
```
csum2() takes 99.8% less time to execute

How many evaluations of cumsum() can be performed per second?
```{r}
cumsum_median <- time2$median[time2$expr == "cumsum"]

1 / (cumsum_median * 1e-6)
```
